reason_summary: No extracted estimate is pre-modern in any substantive sense: demographic-significance.csv records n_cell_a_studies = 0 for PM, and the only PM-tagged row is Basso, Bodenhorn and Cuberes, an 1850 cross-county OLS rated serious on confounding and selection with bank placement conceded to be endogenous. Reading a bank dummy as old-age-security substitution is a speculative mechanism attribution when banks also proxy market access, urbanization and development, which is GRADE's very-low pattern. No decomposition share, slope-sufficiency computation or R-squared exists for PM, so no PROTOCOL 4.2 criterion can be evaluated.

The two moderate-risk quasi-experiments both point the hypothesised way (Danzer and Zyska -0.009, SE 0.003; Rossi and Godard -0.173, SE 0.043), but both are late-twentieth-century developing-country reforms classified FDT-like by a fertility-level rule, not the historical Western FDT; the studies that are actually FDT-era are all serious-risk and split three ways (Fenge and Scheubel -0.453, SE 0.264, insignificant; Guinnane and Streb +0.018, p = 0.22; Galofre-Vila +0.098, SE 0.016, precisely wrong-way). I depart from the chapter on significance: demographic-significance.csv itself records slope_sufficiency as partial_not_formally_scaled with next step 'compute slope sufficiency against observed FDT TFR changes', so none of PROTOCOL 4.2's three criteria has been computed and 'partial' is asserted rather than derived. Escalating because whether the review may state significance verdicts with no underlying computation is a PI call.

Rich-country SDT evidence reduces to one unpublished quasi-experiment, Billari and Galasso, whose completed-fertility estimate (+0.0529, SE 0.0287) is itself insignificant, and the two attempted replications conflict with each other: Shen is negative (-0.169, SE 0.079) while Han is positive (+0.040), both serious-risk and both flagged policy-constrained. I verified that Han's wrong-way estimate sits inside the birth-probability pool at 2.8% weight while Galofre-Vila's precisely-estimated wrong-way completed-fertility estimate was oriented out as broader social spending; re-including it flips that pooled summary from -0.068 to +0.055, so the pool's sign turns on one coding judgment. Significance is not significant on structural grounds rather than a data gap, since mature pension coverage leaves little new variation and the mechanism predicts that retrenchment should have raised fertility; escalating because demographic-significance.csv marks this row needs_human_review = yes and its required step, separating policy-constrained China from rich-country SDT, is undone.

The three designs are genuinely good and consistent, but I could not confirm the panel's provenance claim as stated and what I found is worse: all three are in the retrieved corpus (d1-pool scores 21, 16, 15), so the search did find them, yet none has a row in fulltext-screen.csv, all eight Cell C effect rows are the only ra_verified = no extractions, and the same d1-pool contains directly comparable unextracted candidates including Bratti, Frattini and Scervini (score 17, above two of the three included) and Frattola's 'Parental Retirement and Fertility Decisions Across Family Policy Regimes' with no recorded exclusion reason. A same-signed set selected by hand from a larger on-topic pool cannot earn moderate. On significance I depart from the chapter: the scale check divides individual-level effects by aggregate national TFR changes with no exposure weighting or policy-change scaling, against denominators of 0.097 (Netherlands) and 0.101 (Australia), producing shares of 273% and 149% that fail face validity, and the companion file lists the real scaling as future work, so no PROTOCOL 4.2 criterion exists.
